news.headline: Vidal rushed seven times for 30 yards in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans. He added one catch for six yards on three targets.
news.story: The Chargers continue to use a three-man backfield, an unfriendly fantasy situation and one to avoid when making lineup decisions each week. Vidal has been productive when he does get touches, rushing 36 times for 162 yards (4.5 YPC) and one touchdown across eight games. He's also caught 10 passes for 56 yards and an additional score.

news.headline: Freiermuth (illness) was added to Saturday's injury report and is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Cincinnati.
news.story: Freiermuth is battling through an illness, which puts the veteran tight end's status for Sunday's AFC North tilt in jeopardy, and his official status may not be known until the Steelers announce their list of inactive players approximately 90 minutes before the 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff. If Freiermuth cannot play, then Robert Tonyan would step into a larger role offensively alongside Darnell Washington, and tight end…

news.headline: Lambert-Smith registered one catch (on four targets) for 50 yards in Sunday's loss to Houston.
news.story: Lambert-Smith wasn't exactly prolific in spite of logging a hearty 40 offensive snaps, but he made his one catch count, hauling in a 50-yard reception in the third quarter. However, the woeful Chargers turned the ball over on a fumble two plays later. Lambert-Smith has spent much of the season on IR and has had an inconsistent role when suiting up, but he was deployed pretty heavily Sunday because Ladd McConkey…

news.headline: Hampton rushed 13 times for 60 yards and wasn't targeted in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans.
news.story: Hampton worked as the Chargers' primary rushing option ahead of Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal, who recorded seven carries apiece. The 0-8 Chargers unsurprisingly faced another negative game script, though, and Hampton wasn't involved in the passing game. The 2025 first-round pick continues to disappoint on a surprisingly awful offense that could get even worse should QB Justin Herbert (finger) miss any…

news.headline: Mitchell (hip) does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Ravens.
news.story: Mitchell's practice reps were limited by a hip injury, but he's been officially cleared to play Monday against the team he spent three seasons with from 2023 to 2025. He turned 10 touches into 67 yards during the Chargers' Week 9 loss to the Texans, and Mitchell will continue to operate in a rotational role in the backfield alongside Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal.

news.headline: Mitchell (hip) remained limited at practice Friday.
news.story: It's a new injury for Mitchell, who also was limited Thursday when the Chargers filed their first practice report for the upcoming Monday night game at Baltimore. He'll have some extra motivation, facing his former team in primetime as his current team seeks its first win of the season.

news.headline: Mitchell (hip) was limited at practice Thursday.
news.story: In this past Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans, Mitchell carried seven times for 33 yards and caught three of his four targets for 34 yards while losing a fumble. The 24-year-old currently is operating in a backfield timeshare with Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal in his first campaign with the Chargers, and Mitchell now has two more chances to upgrade his practice participation level ahead of Monday night's game…

news.headline: Hill rushed nine times for 85 yards and a touchdown and brought in all three targets for seven yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night.
news.story: Hill provided the sole offensive highlight of the night for the moribund, Joe Fagnano-led offense, making one cut after getting the handoff from the rookie quarterback halfway through the fourth quarter and bursting through the defense up the right side of the field for a 65-yard touchdown run. Hill's yardage total was both a team- and season-high figure for the veteran change-of-pace back, who should benefit from…

news.headline: Johnston caught one of four targets for a 58-yard touchdown in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans.
news.story: Johnston's long touchdown catch cut the deficit to 38-15 in the fourth quarter. That was the final pass Justin Herbert (finger) completed before exiting the game. If Herbert can't play against the Ravens in Week 10, Johnston would likely find himself catching passes from DJ Uiagalelei. Johnston's 58 receiving yards set a new season high, surpassing his one-catch, 57-yard effort in Week 6, and Sunday's TD was his…

news.headline: Perine rushed 11 times for 43 yards during Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons.
news.story: Perine logged two more carries than Chase Brown in the game, but Brown out-produced him with 57 rushing yards. Perine has continued to operate in a modest role as the Bengals' No. 2 option in the backfield, and he would stand to be a valuable fantasy asset in the case that Brown is forced to miss any action down the road this season.

news.headline: Lane did not draw a target Thursday in a loss to Jacksonville.
news.story: Lane logged 32 offensive snaps, third-most among Baltimore wideouts behind Zay Flowers (37) and Rashod Bateman (35). However, Lane failed to haul in a pass (and to even see a target) for the first time this season. That can be partly attributed to quarterback play, as Ravens starting QB Joe Fagnano threw for just 60 yards. Jacoby Brissett, who Baltimore recently traded for, will likely start behind center in Week…

news.headline: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said that Herbert "should be good to go" for Monday's game at Baltimore after imaging on the quarterback's injured left middle finger returned negative for a fracture, ESPN.com reports.
news.story: Herbert may still have to manage some discomfort in the finger during Monday's contest, but since the injury to his non-throwing hand, he shouldn't be too affected while throwing or handing the ball off. news.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh relayed Monday that Herbert (finger) avoided a fracture in his left middle finger, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.

Harris (calf) was a full participant in Friday's practice.
news.story: After being limited the day before, Harris erased any doubt about his availability for Monday's game at Baltimore. He saw a team-high seven targets on a 79 percent route share last week, catching three passes for a mere six yards in the 44-22 loss to Houston. Harris' volume projection for Week 10 partially depends on Ladd McConkey (back), who didn't play any snaps last week and didn't practice Thursday or Friday.

news.headline: Harris (shoulder) was a limited participant at practice Thursday.
news.story: With teammate Ladd McConkey sidelined by a back injury in Week 9, Harris played 59 of the Chargers' 68 offensive snaps, drawing a team-high seven targets. It seems like he may have picked up an injury of his own along the way though, which makes his availability for Week 10 worth monitoring. He'll have two more chances to manage a full practice before the Chargers publish their last injury report of the week…

news.headline: Harris caught three of seven targets for six yards during Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans.
news.story: Harris failed to take advantage of Ladd McConkey (back) failing to appear in Sunday's game, registering his fewest receiving yards in a game this season. Harris was able to garner a team-high seven targets, which bodes well for his chances of increased production in Week 10 against the Ravens if McConkey remains sidelined.

news.headline: Hibner logged one reception for five yards on two targets in Thursday's loss to Baltimore.
news.story: Hibner ranked second among Baltimore tight ends with 30 offensive snaps, just behind Mark Andrews (32). The former didn't do much with the opportunity, but it was a very quiet game for the Ravens' passing game as a whole, as starting QB Joe Fagnano threw for just 60 yards. Ahead of Week 10, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter noted "I expect (Brissett) to be our starter" next Monday against the Chargers, Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic reports.
news.story: Brissett officially landed with the Ravens in a trade with the Cardinals this past Friday, and he's now on track to assume his new team's starting QB role for the foreseeable future. As a result, Joe Fagnano -- who had a spot start in Week 9 -- will revert to backup status. With regard to franchise signal-caller Lamar Jackson (thumb), who currently is on IR, he's indicated that he plans to return later this season.…

news.headline: Cuevas didn't garner a target in Thursday night's 33-10 loss to the Jaguars.
news.story: Cuevas split time with nine snaps on both offense and special teams. This game marked the fourth time this season that the rookie had zero targets. Prior to Thursday night, the 23-year-old saw multiple targets in four straight games. He will likely have a similar role as the season continues.

Burrow completed 24 of 29 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons. He added seven yards and a TD on three carries.
news.story: It was a nearly flawless performance from Burrow, as he hit Ja'Marr Chase for a 47-yard score in the first quarter and tossed a pair of shorter TDs to Tee Higgins later in the contest. The superstar QB also got into the end zone on a goal-line sneak in the second quarter. It's the fourth straight game in which Burrow has produced at least four touchdowns, an incredible stretch in which he's completed 77.0 percent…

news.headline: Bateman (calf) was listed as a full participant on Friday's practice estimation.
news.story: After being limited at practice Thursday, the starting wideout is in line to face the Chargers on Monday night after being deemed 'FP' on Friday. While Bateman has turned in two consecutive one-catch efforts, there's a chance that working with the team's new QB Jacoby Brissett could spark some added production for the 2021 first-rounder while working alongside top WR Zay Flowers.

news.headline: Bateman (calf) was limited in practice Thursday.
news.story: Bateman now has two more opportunities to practice fully and thus avoid an injury designation prior to Monday night's game against the Chargers. The starting wideout is coming off back-to-back one-catch efforts, but he'll perhaps have an opportunity to bounce back against 0-8 Los Angeles, while working with a new QB in Jacoby Brissett.

news.headline: Bateman caught one of two targets for six yards in Thursday night's 33-10 loss to the Jaguars.
news.story: That's back-to-back one-catch games for Bateman with Joe Fagnano at quarterback for the Ravens. With Zay Flowers also healthy, Bateman has little fantasy appeal in season-long formats, though things could change when Jacoby Brissett takes over as Baltimore's starting quarterback in Week 10.

news.story: Lane logged 32 offensive snaps, third-most among Baltimore wideouts behind Zay Flowers (37) and Rashod Bateman (35). However, Lane failed to haul in a pass (and to even see a target) for the first time this season. That can be partly attributed to quarterback play, as Ravens starting QB Joe Fagnano threw for just 60 yards. news.headline: Njoku (fibula) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Ravens.
news.story: Njoku continues to progress in his recovery from fibula injury that landed him on injured reserve in late September. The veteran tight end turned eight targets into six catches for 67 yards across the first two games of the regular season prior to his injury, and his return would result in a reduced offensive workload for Oronde Gadsden.

news.headline: Njoku (fibula), who is still on IR, was limited in practice Friday.
news.story: Njoku's 21-day practice window was opened Nov. 4, so the Chargers still have plenty of time to activate him. The veteran wideout was limited in all three practices last week and has been limited again Thursday and Friday of this week, so he may need to log a full session Saturday to get the all-clear to suit up Monday in Baltimore. Njoku could provide a boost to a struggling Chargers offense whenever he does return…

news.headline: Njoku (fibula) was a limited participant at the Chargers' practice Thursday.
news.story: Njoku remained limited at the team's first practice of the week as he continues to work his way back from a fibula injury that has sidelined him since Week 2. The tight end was a limited participant at the team's three practices last week, and he'll have two more chances to log a full practice prior to Monday night's matchup with the Ravens.
